records.title: Awkward passing
records.target: Two travelers moving in opposite directions repeatedly choose the same passing side and accidentally get in each other’s way.

coreEvent.assertion: The actors begin with opposing destinationward travel along a shared corridor-like region, without a rendered corridor prop.
Both actors adjust their own routes in an effort to pass; repeated same-side choices interrupt progress.
Obstruction is mutual coordination failure, not one actor repeatedly intercepting an otherwise passive traveler.

allowedElaborations: Vary pause lengths, which traveler initiates each adjustment, path heights and travel distance within the numeric limits.
Show a final successful opposite-side pass only after at least two mutual same-side conflicts have established the event.
Hold an unresolved encounter after the repeated conflicts.
Make braking and intended opposing travel more visible without adding symbols or scenery.

contradictions.assertion: One actor is the persistent deliberate blocker while the other never independently changes its route.
Both actors travel toward a shared destination or one pursues the other.
Only simultaneous rhythmic ornament remains, with no opposing travel or failed passing.
Actors touch, overlap or pass through each other.

targetRubric.complete: The guess describes two people/shapes mutually trying to pass or repeatedly getting in each other’s way while adjusting. No exact phrase, motive or scene setting is required.
targetRubric.partial: The guess identifies mutual obstruction, attempted passing or coordination trouble but omits the relation that distinguishes it from a single blocker.
targetRubric.offTarget: The guess asserts only dancing, pursuit, fighting, or one intentional blocker, with no compatible mutual-passing relation; unrelated/no-interpretation answers are also off target.
acceptedParaphrases: They both keep choosing the same way around.
Trying to get past each other.
An awkward sidewalk shuffle.
likelyConfusions: One is deliberately blocking the other.

records.title: Delayed copying
records.target: One actor copies another actor’s distinct local movements after a visible delay.

coreEvent.assertion: Actor a initiates at least three distinguishable local motion changes before b.
Actor b reproduces the order and relative directions of a’s movements after a visible positive lag.
Both remain in separate local areas; b does not pursue a or try to occupy a’s place.

allowedElaborations: Vary the visible positive lag and irregular pauses while preserving who initiates and the copied sequence.
Use position changes as the main cues; restrained rotation or squash may supplement them.
Keep distinct noncontact anchor zones and vary the path’s shape within each zone.
End with the copier finishing after the initiator has settled.

contradictions.assertion: b initiates the sequence and a copies it.
Both start every motion simultaneously with no discernible leader/lag relation.
The movements are independent sequences rather than ordered imitation.
b follows a through the same global route or approaches a as a pursuer.

targetRubric.complete: The guess identifies one actor copying, mimicking or repeating the other after it acts; explicit numerical delay is unnecessary.
targetRubric.partial: The guess notices similar repeated moves or a follow-the-leader relation without making the imitation/order clear.
targetRubric.offTarget: The guess describes only synchronized dance, independent exercise, pursuit or role-reversed imitation, without a compatible copying relation.
acceptedParaphrases: One is copying the other.
The second shape keeps mimicking the first.
Follow the leader, a beat late.

records.title: Making room
records.target: Two actors open a space between them so a third approaching actor can join.

coreEvent.assertion: a and b initially form a close pair, while c approaches from outside their line.
The pair increases the gap before c enters it, making the approach physically possible under the noncontact policy.
c enters and remains between them; the final arrangement accommodates all three rather than driving c away.

allowedElaborations: Let the pair notice/react sequentially or together, provided the opening precedes entry.
Let c hesitate before entering or let the pair settle modestly inward after arrival.
Use different approach directions only if the pair/joiner relationship and final inclusion remain clear.
Hold the final three-person grouping long enough to read.

contradictions.assertion: The pair repeatedly closes c’s approached gap or keeps c outside.
The pair flees and abandons c rather than leaving an occupied three-actor grouping.
c forces the pair apart through contact or overlap.
The pair opens only after c has already passed through them.

targetRubric.complete: The guess describes making space, opening a place or moving apart to let someone join; a welcome/friendship motive is optional.
targetRubric.partial: The guess describes the pair moving apart or a third joining but does not connect opening the space with the entry.
targetRubric.offTarget: The guess describes excluding, chasing away, attacking or fleeing the third, with no compatible accommodation relation.
acceptedParaphrases: They make room for the other one.
Opening a gap so it can join them.
The third is welcomed into the line.
likelyConfusions: The two move away because they are afraid of it.

records.title: Tagging along
records.target: One actor follows another actor’s route with a comfortable delay.

coreEvent.assertion: a travels a route with at least one meaningful turn.
b subsequently retraces the same global route in the same direction.
The following retains separation and does not become an attempt to catch or escape.

allowedElaborations: Use one or two clear turns and a brief leader pause.
Maintain a stable comfortable route-following gap.
Let b wait when a stops, rather than closing into contact.

contradictions.assertion: b intercepts, attacks, overtakes or corners a.
The actors move only in parallel local zones with copied gestures instead of following the same route.
a is following b throughout.

targetRubric.complete: The guess identifies one following or tagging along behind the other along its route.
targetRubric.partial: The guess identifies shared travel or one actor behind the other without the route-following dependency.
targetRubric.offTarget: The guess asserts a chase, interception or local copying only, without compatible calm following.
acceptedParaphrases: One is following the other.
Tagging along.
Following the same path behind it.
likelyConfusions: They copy movements from separate places.

records.title: Trying to catch up

coreEvent.assertion: Both move in a shared travel direction with b visibly behind a.
b moves so that the travel gap narrows after being visibly established.
b rejoins alongside or close behind with safe clearance, and a does not flee from b.

allowedElaborations: Let a pause briefly near the end while b finishes closing the gap.
Let both continue side by side after rejoining.
Vary b’s speed without excessive bouncing or changing the direction relation.

contradictions.assertion: a continually escapes or a pursuit ends with a cornered victim.
b overtakes in a contest instead of rejoining.
The gap never narrows after being established.

targetRubric.complete: The guess describes trying to catch up, rejoining or avoiding falling behind.
targetRubric.partial: The guess identifies faster/slower shared travel or a growing/narrowing gap without the rejoining relation.

acceptedParaphrases: The one behind is catching up.
Trying not to be left behind.
They get back together while moving.
likelyConfusions: One is chasing the other away.

coreEvent.assertion: c approaches a passable opening between a and b.
The pair closes that opening before c can enter, and c stops or changes its approach.

contradictions.assertion: The pair opens and c successfully joins the group.
c simply happens to miss an unrelated moving formation with no response dependency.
Physical contact or violence is used to establish exclusion.

a returns to the lead immediately without a sustained change.
The actors reverse directions rather than exchange leadership.
